chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
The time of Maghrib is from when the sun sets until the stars become interwoven.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose setting marks the beginning of Maghrib time
key_terms.النُّجُومُ: the stars, whose visible spread marks the end point mentioned here
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the sunset prayer; here, its appointed time
key_terms.تَغِيبُ: disappears or sets, referring to the sun
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the prescribed time or period for an act

ai.seo_question: What is the time of Maghrib prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the time window for salat al-Maghrib. It begins at sunset and continues until the stars become densely visible in the sky, indicating the limit of its time.
